scope.purpose: Navigate to another page or resource from inside text, as an underlined word or phrase that reads with the sentence around it.
useCases: A link inside a paragraph, a help text, a table cell or a message, taking the surrounding typography.
A standalone text link (See all, Learn more) placed by the layout, still underlined.
An external destination that opens in a new tab, with a visible arrow and an announced suffix.
A link inside a colored context (status message, inverse surface) that keeps the context color with tone inherit.
exclusions: Navigation to a task with a control appearance: Button with href.
A disabled link: a destination that cannot be followed is plain text.
Leading or trailing icons other than the external indicator.
Distinct visited color; size or weight options (the context decides typography).
Routing: the application's router intercepts navigation; the component renders a native link.
alternatives: Button (with href) for a call to action or navigation to a task.
IconButton (with href) for an icon-only navigation control.
Breadcrumb, Tabs, Pagination (wave 4) for structured navigation.

checks.note: Schema, consistency and token coverage (8 paths) in 18 contexts; check-foundations passes (383 roles, 1836 contrast checks, 0 failures).

108 contrast records on the contrastScope backdrops in 18 contexts, 0 failures. The component report measures only the focus ring (Link binds content without a surface role); color.content.link on the six backdrops was measured separately: 4.93 to 7.83 except surface.muted in dark (3.30 to 3.46), see open decision 1.

decisionsTaken: label is a required string, like Button, rather than free children: the accessible name is then known to the component (needed to append the external suffix) and Figma maps it to a text property.

Underlined in every state (WCAG 1.4.1, use of color): the hover and pressed feedback thickens the underline from border.width.default (1 px) to border.width.strong (2 px) instead of changing the color, so no new color token is needed; no transition.
One color role, color.content.link (approved), and tone inherit for colored contexts; no visited color in an application context.
No size prop and no typography role: a link takes the font of the text it sits in.

external groups three facts that belong together: a new browsing context without opener, a visible arrow glyph (Phosphor ArrowUpRight, inline SVG in the component folder, attributed, per the icon decision) and an announced suffix externalLabel (default "opens in a new tab", a string prop so that it can be translated).
Focus indicator drawn around each line box (an outline, so a wrapped link gets one ring per line) with radius.indicator corners: radius.focus (concentric with controls) is too round for text.
No Bits UI primitive: a native anchor carries every semantic needed.

openDecisions.question: color.content.link reaches only 3.30 to 3.46:1 on color.surface.muted in dark (all three brands); 4.94 or more on the other neutral backdrops. Change the dark link color?
openDecisions.proposal: Recommended (A): foundations amendment, color.content.link in dark from color.palette.accent.400 to color.palette.accent.300: 4.80 to 4.95 on muted, 7.17 or more elsewhere; the inventory pair content.link / surface.muted is added. Alternative (B): keep the value and declare surface.muted out of the Link contrastScope in dark (use tone inherit there).

openDecisions.question: Should the external indicator and its announced suffix stay tied to the new-tab behavior (one external option)?
openDecisions.proposal: Yes: an external destination in an application usually opens in a new tab, and announcing the new tab is what users need to know; a link to another site in the same tab is a plain link.

nextAction: Contract gate (grouped with IconButton and Badge): reviewer decides the dark link color (open decision 1) and the external option (2); then record the approval and start the implementation.
implementationNotes: Markup: <a class="ggb-link" data-tone href> with the label, and when external target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" plus the glyph (aria-hidden) and a visually hidden suffix. The glyph is joined to the last word with a no-break so it never starts a line.
Underline through text-decoration (thickness from the tokens, text-underline-offset from-font); focus with outline on the inline box so it follows each line.
